clue.text: Strip-joints opening today

parts.note: a joint is a seedy bar or club, as is a dive

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here taken from today

explanation.surface: A strip club starting up for business this very day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strip-joints' looks like one compound, but the hyphen splits it: 'Strip' is the definition and 'joints' gives DIVES.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip someone of something is to deprive or dispossess them of it.

clue.text: Down payments for measures of coal, for example

explanation.surface: Initial instalments paid for loads of coal.
explanation.definitionFit: Money paid up front to secure a purchase; also natural layers of mineral laid down in the earth, like coal seams.

clue.text: French verse form broadcast after six

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
to relay a programme is to transmit or broadcast it

explanation.surface: A French poem going out on air after six o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the broadcast word after the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A short medieval French poem with linked rhymes on two sounds.

clue.text: By writing this, zoo can be made so — with sudden emphasis

parts.words: By writing this, zoo can be made so
parts.note: turn the word zoo into so by writing S in place of Z and keeping one O

explanation.surface: An odd instruction about spelling a word, ending with a musical direction.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue describes how to edit 'zoo' into 'so'; the instruction itself, spelt as one word, is the musical term.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian musical marking telling the player to accent a note or chord forcefully and abruptly.

clue.text: Travelling-clock?

parts.note: not a clock for taking on trips, but a dial that clocks up the distance a vehicle travels

explanation.definitionFit: A dashboard instrument measuring miles covered, which motorists say 'clocks' the mileage.

clue.text: Gear-changing practice for road show?

parts.note: suggests a driver practising gear changes before a road test, but means the full-costume run-through before a touring show opens

explanation.surface: A learner driver rehearsing gear changes before a test on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: The final rehearsal of a play in full costume, where actors practise changing their outfits.

clue.text: Chap to travel for tropical fruit

parts.note: a chap is a man
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: A fellow setting off to fetch something from the tropics.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet orange-fleshed stone fruit grown in hot countries.

clue.text: Ground where there is no parking for a water-tortoise

indicators.note: tells us a letter is missing from the reptile's name

parts.note: a terrapin is a freshwater turtle
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A patch of land where no car may park, set aside for a pond turtle.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is land considered by its physical features, the lie of the ground.

clue.text: Standard text-book for a senior lecturer

explanation.surface: The set book recommended by a senior member of a university.
explanation.definitionFit: A school book of graded passages for learning to read; also a British university rank just below professor.

clue.text: Perhaps the good marry if she waves her wand

definitions.text: Perhaps the good marry if she waves her wand

indicators.note: a wave of a magic wand transforms things, so the letters before it are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: In a fairy tale, virtuous heroines get wed when a magical helper casts her spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'she waves her wand' rearranges THE GOOD MARRY IF, and the whole clue also describes the pantomime character who arranges Cinderella's match.
explanation.definitionFit: The magical guardian of fairy tales who grants wishes, as for Cinderella going to the ball.

clue.text: Country home of three belles we hear

definitions.text: Country home of three belles we hear

parts.words: Country home of three belles we hear
parts.note: belles sounds like Bells: the Brontë sisters wrote as Currer, Ellis and Acton Bell, and lived at Haworth in a clergyman's house

explanation.surface: A rural house where three pretty girls are said to live.
explanation.walkthrough: The Brontë sisters (Charlotte, Emily and Anne) published under the pen-name Bell and grew up in Haworth, a Yorkshire village, where their father was the parish priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman's official residence, like the vicarage where the Brontë family lived.

clue.text: Bellini's work has the usual cut

indicators.note: the last letter is cut away from the word for usual

parts.note: normal means usual

explanation.surface: A Bellini opera is performed with the customary abridgements.
explanation.definitionFit: An 1831 opera by Vincenzo Bellini about a Druid priestess.

clue.text: Let's change to nothing short of mineral water

indicators.note: the letters of let's change into a new order
short means the word is missing its final letter

parts.note: zero means nothing

explanation.surface: Let's swap our drinks for nothing but fizzy water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges LETS into SELT; 'short' docks the final O from ZERO to leave ZER.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturally effervescent spring water, originally from Selters in Germany; also used for soda water generally.

clue.text: Charge for keeping goods and silver in warehouse

indicators.note: the metal is placed inside the building word

parts.note: a store is a warehouse
AG is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Money paid to keep stock and silverware in a depot.
explanation.definitionFit: A fee charged for warehousing goods is itself called storage.

clue.text: Sell the dummy — touchdown possible

explanation.surface: A rugby player feints a pass and may score.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby, selling a dummy is faking a pass, and a try is scored by touching the ball down.
explanation.definitionFit: To attempt a deception or bluff; also a chance of scoring a rugby try.

clue.text: Fag-end got bent in picking up' the pieces

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, here of fag

parts.note: leaning means tilted or bent over

explanation.surface: A cigarette stub lying crooked among scraps someone is collecting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fag-end' reads as a cigarette butt (fag is British slang for cigarette) but gives the last letter of 'Fag'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gathering grain left by reapers, and hence collecting scraps of information bit by bit.

clue.text: Strange one brightened this classical old age

definitions.note: an adjective describing the age, here standing for it

indicators.note: strange signals the letters of one are rearranged

parts.note: lit means brightened
hic is Latin, the classical language, for this

explanation.surface: An odd person cheered up by this ancient era.
explanation.definitionFit: The later Stone Age, when farming and polished tools appeared.

clue.text: One is set to drain off water when royal egg is cooked

definitions.text: One is set to drain off water

indicators.note: cooking an egg alters it, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A drainage fixture installed when a king's breakfast egg is prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved grotesque spout on a church roof that throws rainwater clear of the wall.

clue.text: Pair in light kiss and cuddle

indicators.note: the pair goes inside the word for a light

parts.note: a candle is a light
two rings or round letters, OO, a pair like spectacles

explanation.surface: A couple embracing in the soft glow.
explanation.definitionFit: To canoodle is to fondle and pet amorously.

clue.text: Railmen taking part in minor complaint

indicators.note: only part of the words railmen taking is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Railway workers joining in with a petty grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' tempts toward a workers' grievance, but here it means an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: An ailment is a mild illness or disorder.

clue.text: Is "A" so out of tune we need a musical alternative?

indicators.note: music out of tune is wrong, so the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Is the note A so badly off pitch that we need another version?
explanation.definitionFit: Italian for 'or', marking an optional alternative passage in a score.

clue.text: Flight engineer concerned with pitch?

parts.note: sounds like an aircraft crew member, but a cricket bowler varies the ball's flight and relies on the pitch to turn it

explanation.surface: An aviation engineer worried about the angle of the aircraft's nose.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a slow bowler 'flights' the ball (throws it high) and makes it turn off the pitch, the strip of grass between the wickets.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow bowler in cricket who makes the ball turn sharply off the ground.

clue.text: This wader has an octave range

indicators.note: range suggests rearranging, with the octave's letters set out afresh

explanation.surface: A shorebird whose song spans eight notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A black-and-white long-legged shorebird with an upturned bill, emblem of the RSPB.

clue.text: Mount that is dangerous when : active…

definitions.text: Mount that is dangerous when : active

parts.words: Mount that is dangerous when : active
parts.note: a mountain posing a threat only when it is erupting

explanation.definitionFit: A mountain with a vent through which lava and gas erupt.

clue.text: Shock for a Scandinavian mountaineer

indicators.note: in a down clue a mountaineer climbs, so the northern person goes upward and is read backwards

parts.note: a Lapp is a native of Lapland in northern Scandinavia

explanation.surface: A terrible fright for a Nordic climber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mountaineer' reverses LAPP to PPAL, rising up the column.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to horrify or dismay.

clue.text: … abusing fence, perhaps

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a volcano rails like someone hurling abuse at a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: Railing at someone is scolding them bitterly; railings also form a barrier of bars around property.

clue.text: Cold store base

parts.note: C is the tap abbreviation for cold
a heap is a pile or store of things

explanation.surface: A refrigerated warehouse at a military base.
explanation.definitionFit: Base can mean low in worth or vulgar, as does cheap.

clue.text: The, unenlightened inflame Professor Higgins

parts.note: to heat is to inflame
Henry Higgins is the phonetics professor in Shaw's Pygmalion and My Fair Lady

explanation.surface: Benighted people anger Professor Higgins.
explanation.definitionFit: Heathenry denotes heathens collectively, people without religious enlightenment.

clue.text: Serving as guardian yet ultra-changeable

indicators.note: changeable means the letters may be altered into another order

explanation.surface: A protector who is nonetheless extremely fickle.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutelary means protective, acting as a guardian or patron.

clue.text: Damage to church is seldom met with.

parts.note: to scar is to damage
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Vandalism of a church rarely happens.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scarce is rare, found only infrequently.
